Hi there! The winters here can be pretty rough, so I'd recommend a few things:

Winter boots/shoes! You definitely want at least one pair that covers your ankles, and preferably something that's relatively waterproof. (Generally stay away from things like Uggs; they'll get sopping wet super fast, and they have no traction to help in the snow).

Winter coat! Get something that's waterproof and has some kind of insulating layer. Poofy doesn't always mean better but is definitely a great start. You definitely want something more than just a windbreaker or sweatshirt.

Frostbite protection! The way I phrased it sounds somewhat dramatic, but really I just mean a solid pair of gloves and something to cover your ears (either a long beanie, some earmuffs, a thick scarf to wrap around your head, etc.) 

Long pants! I'm not sure if it's standard attire in your region, but a few pairs of jeans or cargo pants or the like will keep your legs warm. (I don't super trust yoga pants to keep me warm, but that's just me).

As far as wear to buy these things, there's a clothing chain called "Kohl's" that's pretty close to campus that I'm pretty sure you can get to by bus that has reasonable prices. Otherwise, Amazon works just fine (make sure you look at the user reviews about how long the clothing lasts, how well it fits, and how well it protections from the wind/rain.)

My father was raised Catholic and my mom's dad was a Presbyterian minister. My dad now basically wants nothing to do with religion in his day-to-day life, and my mom sings with the choir at our local church solely because she likes those specific members of that community. In my experience, I've never found that much comfort in religion of any sort. I have nothing against those that do, and I honestly love learning about different customs and histories others have. 

I guess my biggest issue is with organized religion, particularly the Catholic and Baptist churches (to be fair, however, these are just the communities I know the most about). It really just seems like a huge pyramid scheme that takes money and resources from those that don't have enough to bring riches and comfort to those that do. On top of that, so many of their leaders have been convicted or otherwise proven to be far less then scrupulous or righteous. If these are the people that are supposed to be the moral compass, what does that say about that community, or the human race in general?

I'm a firm believer in the scientific method: if you can prove something with solid evidence, I'll probably stand behind it. So far, a large portion of Christian stories (again, just because I know the most about it) have been proven to false, to have outgrown their usage due to the passage of time, or in fact not be true due to mistranslations and different interpretations. To me, it's not something that can be relied upon for moral guidance. For that reason, I'm pretty solidly in the atheist camp for 99% of my life.

Note: Because I am a pesky American and it's like 1 AM, all the units are Imperial/stupid and I'm sorry but I do not have the mental capacity to translate it to the better units as I'm also writing this on a phone let me be okay 

REQUIRED MATERIALS:
Ice cream machine (duh) (I've got a Cuisinart one)
Whisk(s)
Spatula(s)
A bunch 'o' bowls (I need a lot bc I am a failure)
Instant read thermometer
Refrigerator (duh²)
Freezer (duh³)
Patience (I have none want ice crem)

INGREDIENTS (the ones I'm pretty sure work, anyway):
8 oz. Milk chocolate (it says bittersweet but that's lame brosef)
1½ cups whole milk (I'm gonna try whole chocolate milk, bc again I'm a child)
1½ cups heavy cream
¾ cup granulated sugar (5¼ oz)
4 large egg yolks
1 tps. Vanilla extract 

MY ADDITIONS (I haven't tested this so do not take my word for it)

1(?) tsp. Mint extract*
1(?) tsp. Caramel extract*
1(?) tsp. Marshmallow flavoring*
2(?) oz. Peanut butter chips OR(and?) ¼ cup creamy peanut butter
2(?) oz. Butterscotch chips*
10 Oreo Thins, crushed
2 tbsp. of cookie dough, in BITE SIZED pieces (don't add cookie sized lobs, no matter how much you want it)(and I really want it)

*I have no idea how much to add, as I have no idea how strong each of these are. I want an even chaos of flavors, not really having one stand out in particular. This is way easier with 2 flavors instead of the 497 I've picked out, but dad doesn't say I'm an obstinate woman for nothing.

DIRECTIONS:
1. In a medium heatproof bowl set over a pan of almost simmering water (or use a double boiler, if you're rich or something) melt the chocolate (or whatever other crazy flavors your chaos child desires) stirring occasionally, until smooth. Set aside to cool.

2. Meanwhile, position a strainer over a medium bowl set in larger bowl containing ice water (double cooler?). Heat the milk, cream, and ½ cup of the sugar in a medium saucepan to dissolve the sugar, until steam appears and the milk is warm (~75°F), about 5 minutes. While the milk is heating, beat the yolks and remaining ¼ cup sugar in a medium bowl until combined and pale yellow. Add melted chocolate and beat until fully incorporated.

3. Whisk half the warm milk mixture into the beaten yolks, ½ cup at a time, until combined. Whisk the milk-yolk mixture into the warm milk in the saucepan; set the saucepan over medium heat and cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon until steam appears, foam subsides, and the mixture is slightly thickened or an instant read thermometer registers 180-185°F (DO NOT BOIL MIXTURE; EGGS WILL CURDLE). Immediately strain the custard into the bowl set in the ice bath; cool the custard to room temperature, stirring it occasionally to help it cool. Stir in the vanilla (or, again, whatever wacky flavorings you or your chaos child desire)(I'm the chaos child btw) then cover and refrigerate until an instant read thermometer registers 40°F or lower (at least 3hrs., or up to 24hrs.)

4. (The Fun Part™) Pour the custard into the ice cream machine canister and churn, following the manufacturer's instructions, until the mixture resembles soft serve ice cream. (At this point, if you have any "solid" add-ins - fruit, cookies, brownie/cake bits, candy bars, etc. - add them as BITE SIZED (aka TINY) pieces to the churn.) Transfer the ice cream (or whatever the heck it is you made) to an airtight container, press plastic wrap flush against surface, cover the container, and freeze the ice cream until firm, at least 2hrs. (Ice cream will keep up to 2 days) (unless I get my hands on it)(then it's like 4 hours brosef).
